question: For normal J293/T8103 dart-apcie0, does DART-register MMIO require PCIe PHY/port RUN or only its PMGR/bus-clock domain?
answer: The pinned normal Linux DART probe does not explicitly require PHY, PERST, port RUN or endpoint link-up. It enables declared clocks and reads parameters. This is not evidence that the four PMGR words alone make a cold/reset normal APCIE DART aperture safe: the exact DART Linux clock/power provider declarations are missing locally, normal pinned m1n1 kboot already initializes PCIe, and the saved ADT has no independent DART clock/reset contract. The current all-PCIe readiness guard is conservative; its necessity is not proven, but its removal is not justified by these sources.

separation_from_runtime.fact: Four PMGR predicate checks passed, then the fifth read found PHY reset asserted and its request/ack predicate incomplete. The sampler stopped with zero DART reads.
separation_from_runtime.limits: Later RC/APPCLK/PERST/RUN fields were never read; their zero snapshot fields are not hardware state. The run cannot measure which of those signals the DART aperture actually needs. No current or earlier refusal is relabeled SAMPLED.

primary_evidence.finding: Normal vs tunneled is selected from the DT parent name. For the normal path: map >=0x4000 resource, get IRQ, devm_clk_bulk_get_all, clk_bulk_prepare_enable, runtime-PM bookkeeping, then read PARAMS1/PARAMS2. No pcie_init, PHY register, link-status or endpoint PERST test is performed by this probe.

The actual clock list comes from firmware metadata/providers. pm_runtime_get_noresume plus set_active does not by itself establish a particular physical power-up handshake; exact platform/PM-domain attachment and DT providers must be known. Number of clocks may be zero. Absence of a direct test is not a cold-read safety guarantee.

After parameter/profile reads the driver may reset/write the DART, then registers its IOMMU. Consumer device_link_add uses the DART as runtime-PM supplier. This dependency makes the DART available before a consumer uses it; it does not prove DART probes before all host/bootloader PCIe setup.

Normal T8103 host probe resolves port GPIO dependencies, initializes MSI and calls generic PCI-host setup. setup_port may inherit a live link; otherwise setup_link enables APPCLK, asserts endpoint GPIO PERST, programs refclk, releases internal PORT_PERST and endpoint GPIO, and waits PORT_STATUS_READY. LTSSM/link training is distinct and later. There is no normal-DART-specific access guard here; generic PCI core/DT ordering is not fully present in this partial source acquisition.

The pinned normal kboot handoff calls tunables_apply_static, clk_init, USB init and pcie_init before handing off. Therefore a normal Linux probe can run with PCIe PHY/APPCLK/port already initialized; Linux driver source alone cannot reproduce the survey cold/reset starting state.

m1n1 first enables APCIE ADT clock-gate domains, applies shared tunables, requests/acks PHY clocks and releases PHY reset, starts PHYIF, then each port APPCLK, internal reset release and RUN poll. It does not independently read/verify normal DART reachability between these phases. The sequence shows how PCIe is initialized, not minimal DART prerequisites.
pmgr_power_enable recurses through domain parents; pmgr_adt_find_devices consumes clock-gates. No DART-specific clock mapping is inferred when dart-apcie0 has no such property.

dart_init and dart_init_adt assume the aperture is accessible. T8020 immediately reads CONFIG then may write stream/TTBR/TCR/invalidation state. No power or PCIe guard is present. This low-level mutating helper is not a safe survey or evidence of prerequisite sufficiency.
from_adt resolves the register address and constructs a backend; it neither checks nor enables power.

Constructor already reads ENABLED_STREAMS; initialize mutates translations. Even constructing this convenience object is not source-only or a harmless way to test the hypothesis. No imports/execution were used in this review.
HV entry calls pcie_shutdown. This differs from normal kboot and cannot inherit its initialized-state assumption without evidence.

Shutdown is gated by in-process initialized state; when entered, it clears per-port reset-disable/APPCLK and PHY clock requests. A call does not establish what prior firmware or another proxy image initialized. Survey001 actual guard reads remain the authority for the five observed fields.

PCIe-C/tunneled DART has explicit asynchronous-abort and APPCLK/resume-order constraints and skips unsafe parameter reads. Restore can precede downstream link training, but this is a different aperture/profile. Neither its hazards nor its sufficiency rules can be silently transferred to normal dart-apcie0.
The explicit host-before-DART PM link is inside the PCIe-C tunnel path, not normal T8103 APCIE. It is not proof that normal DART requires RUN, nor that it is independent of APPCLK.

PMGR target/actual/reset/disable state is a meaningful domain guard. Externally-clocked domains explicitly permit clock-gated actual state while requesting active, demonstrating that a generic PMGR operation is not a universal local-clock contract. This survey instead requires actual active and rejects AUTO/reset/disable, but the normal DART clock relation still needs separate evidence.

saved_ADT_evidence.decoder: Existing bounded parse_adt extracted as Python AST; no m1n1/transport import. Selected nodes only.
saved_ADT_evidence.normal_DART: /arm-io/dart-apcie0 is dart,t8020, normal aperture0x681008000/0x4000, sibling of apcie under arm-io, manual-availability=1. No clock-gates, power-gates, clocks, power-domains or dependencies properties.

APCIE_domains.PMGR_ancestry: APCIE77 -> IMX32; APCIE_GP97 -> APCIE77; PCIE_REF29 has no parent in the validated table. These are APCIE node declarations, not a separately declared DART domain.

saved_ADT_evidence.bridge_functions: pci-bridge0 function-dart_force_active/request_sid/release_sid/self each point to dart-apcie0 phandle with an operation selector. They describe software calls; no implementation in the local pinned sources defines F-act or manual-availability as an electrical clock/reset prerequisite. Do not treat these as a Linux dependency cell or success permission.
saved_ADT_evidence.reference: integrations/puredarwin/m1-dart-survey/board.c:50-114 validates identities/ranges/APCIE domains. Absence of DART clock properties independently checked in actual saved blob.

prerequisite_matrix.source_support: Established from actual saved ADT and T8103 driver match.
prerequisite_matrix.sufficiency: Necessary identity constraint; not bus access safety.

prerequisite_matrix.item: Four PMGR domains active, reset/disable/AUTO absent
prerequisite_matrix.source_support: Established APCIE declarations and observed successful predicates.
prerequisite_matrix.sufficiency: Good conservative prerequisite; no source proves it is sufficient for DART.

prerequisite_matrix.item: Shared PHY request/ACK and PHY reset released
prerequisite_matrix.source_support: Explicit PCIe initialization steps; current survey guard.
prerequisite_matrix.sufficiency: Not established as normal DART MMIO requirement. Fails in actual survey; no DART read attempted.

prerequisite_matrix.item: RC PHYIF RUN, port APPCLK and internal PORT_PERST release, PORT_STATUS_RUN
prerequisite_matrix.source_support: Explicit host-controller startup steps. APPCLK is a proven DART dependency only for the separately scoped tunneled path.
prerequisite_matrix.sufficiency: Unproven for normal aperture; all unobserved in survey001 after early refusal.

prerequisite_matrix.item: Endpoint GPIO PERST released, radio power or PCIe LINK_UP
prerequisite_matrix.source_support: Consumer link startup requirements, distinct from local DART MMIO and from internal port-reset bit.
prerequisite_matrix.sufficiency: No normal DART source requires link-up. That absence does not prove safe reads with local core/PHY reset asserted; external endpoint reset must not be conflated with internal port or PHY reset.

missing_primary_evidence: Exact pinned arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple/t8103.dtsi and board includes, plus applicable DART/PCIe/clock/power bindings, are not in the acquired local reference set. No fetch was performed. Need to resolve normal dart0 clocks/power-domains to their provider and ancestry rather than reuse APCIE or keyboard phandles.

The partial Linux source set lacks generic platform/genpd/of-IOMMU probe-order implementations needed to prove actual normal-DART power and clock setup/order. No runtime probe-order trace is present in the saved survey.

No local specification or proven cold/reset experiment establishes the reset-tree/bus-clock relation for normal0x681008000. APPCLK vs shared PHY vs internal PORT_RESET may affect access independently of endpoint PERST.
No hardware bus-fault containment/timeout guarantee follows from a whitelisted offset or an IOMap read-only mapping; a synchronous load can still fault or hang on an unclocked aperture.
recommendation: Keep frozen survey002 and its truthful refusal unchanged. Do not call pcie_init or weaken checks on the strength of Linux not checking PHY explicitly.

Resolve the missing exact DT/provider and local clock/reset contract before proposing a separate read-only guard revision. Existing retained snapshots may help, but any source acquisition or hardware observation is separate authorization.

If those facts support DART-only MMIO, propose an isolated candidate with no PMGR/PHY/link writes and endpoints kept in their proven reset state, explicit power/clock ownership for the whole read interval, bounded observation and failure evidence. A candidate would still require independent review and explicit hardware authorization.
not_done: No guard or production/source changes, no init, no pcie_init, no register or device access, no source fetch, no builds, no SSH.
No DART-only read has been authorized or executed by this analysis. No register-value allowlist is used as bus-safety proof.
